title: Safe Use of AI Tools and Third-Party Apps
summary: How to use AI tools, cloud services and third-party apps safely within the firm's policies, avoid shadow IT and data leakage, and apply the programme to practical scenarios.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How to use AI tools, cloud services and third-party apps safely within the firm's policies, avoid shadow IT and data leakage, and apply the programme to practical scenarios.
Learning Objectives: Apply the firm's policies on AI tools, cloud services and third-party apps
Recognise the data leakage, accuracy and security risks of unapproved tools
Apply the programme to realistic cyber, data and resilience scenarios
Syllabus: Approved versus unapproved tools: shadow IT and personal accounts
What never goes into an AI tool: customer, confidential and personal data
Browser extensions, messaging apps and file-sharing services
Workshop: what would you do? Cyber, data and disruption scenarios
Intended Audience: All staff in regulated firms, including new joiners, contractors and temporary staff with access to the firm's systems
Front-office, operations, technology, HR, finance and support staff who handle customer data or critical processes
Line managers responsible for secure working practices and continuity arrangements in their teams
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: No technical background is required. The programme is suitable for new joiners and as annual refresher training.
Core Reading: ISO/IEC (2022), ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Information Security, Cybersecurity and Privacy Protection – Information Security Management Systems – Requirements
ISO (2019), ISO 22301:2019 Security and Resilience – Business Continuity Management Systems – Requirements
